reason: Key correct (Art VI Sec 2); added citation and teaching fields.

fields.explanation: Article VI, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the Senate is composed of 24 senators elected at large by the qualified voters of the Philippines.
fields.hint: Think of the number of senatorial slots on a full ballot, which is twice the number elected every three years.
fields.whyA: 21 is not in the Constitution; it may come from confusing the count with the number of members of other bodies.
fields.whyB: 22 is a guess just under the real figure; the Constitution fixes it at 24.
fields.whyC: 23 is one short; the Senate has 24 seats, 12 elected every three years.
fields.explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 2 ng 1987 Constitution, 24 senators ang bumubuo sa Senate, at elected at large sila ng mga botante sa buong Pilipinas.
fields.hintTl: Isipin mo kung ilan ang senador na binoboto every three years, tapos i-double mo.

reason: Key correct; explanation now cites Art XIV Sec 6 and notes Tagalog trap.

fields.explanation: Article XIV, Section 6 of the 1987 Constitution states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino, which shall be further developed and enriched on the basis of existing Philippine and other languages.
fields.hint: The 1987 Constitution uses a name that is not tied to any single regional language.
fields.whyA: English is an official language for communication and instruction (Art XIV Sec 7), not the national language.
fields.whyC: Tagalog is a regional language that Filipino is largely based on, but the Constitution names Filipino, not Tagalog.
fields.whyD: Cebuano is a major regional language, not the national language.
fields.explanationTl: Ayon sa Article XIV, Section 6 ng 1987 Constitution, Filipino ang national language natin. Hindi Tagalog, kahit malaki ang base nito sa Tagalog.
fields.hintTl: Yung pangalan na ginamit ng Constitution ay hindi pangalan ng isang rehiyon lang.

reason: Key correct (Art VI Sec 23(1)); replaced non-plausible 'Minority' distractor.

fields.explanation: Article VI, Section 23(1) of the 1987 Constitution provides that Congress, by a vote of two-thirds of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately, has the sole power to declare the existence of a state of war.
fields.hint: Declaring war is a grave act, so it needs a supermajority, the same fraction used to override a presidential veto.
fields.whyB: One-half (a simple majority) is too low for an act as grave as declaring war.
fields.whyC: Three-quarters is not used here; it is higher than what Section 23 requires.
fields.whyD: Three-fifths is not the fraction in Section 23; the Constitution requires two-thirds.
fields.explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 23(1), kailangan ng two-thirds vote ng both Houses, in joint session pero voting separately, para mag-declare ng state of war ang Congress.
fields.hintTl: Mabigat na desisyon ang pag-declare ng war, kaya supermajority ang kailangan. Pareho ito sa fraction para ma-override ang veto ng President.

reason: Key correct (Art VI Sec 4); fixed garbled stem wording.

fields.text: Under the 1987 Constitution, how long is the term of office of a senator?
fields.explanation: Article VI, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the term of office of senators is six years, and no senator may serve more than two consecutive terms.
fields.hint: A senator's term is twice as long as the term of a member of the House of Representatives.
fields.whyA: 3 years is the term of a member of the House of Representatives (Art VI Sec 7), not a senator.
fields.whyB: 4 years is not a term used for senators under the 1987 Constitution.
fields.whyC: 5 years is not a constitutional term for senators; it may be confused with other fixed terms.
fields.explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 4, six years ang term ng senador, at hanggang two consecutive terms lang ang pwede.
fields.hintTl: Doble ang term ng senador kumpara sa congressman.

reason: Key correct; added article citations; difficulty set to 1 (basic recall).

fields.explanation: The 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in Congress (Art VI), executive power in the President (Art VII), and judicial power in the Supreme Court and lower courts (Art VIII).
fields.hint: Think of separation of powers: one branch makes laws, one carries them out, one interprets them.
fields.whyA: These are institutions, not branches; the Senate is part of Congress, so the legislature is counted twice.
fields.whyB: These are forms of government, not branches of government.
fields.whyD: The Senate is part of the Legislature, and the executive branch is missing entirely.
fields.explanationTl: Separation of powers: Legislative (Congress, Art VI), Executive (President, Art VII), at Judicial (Supreme Court at lower courts, Art VIII).
fields.hintTl: Isa ang gumagawa ng batas, isa ang nagpapatupad, at isa ang nag-i-interpret.

reason: Vague stem and wrong citation (Art XII); rewritten to the exact Art II Sec 16 wording.

fields.text: Under Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution, the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a ____ ecology.
fields.explanation: Article II, Section 16 of the 1987 Constitution states that the State shall protect and advance the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.
fields.hint: The phrase pairs the idea of nature in equilibrium with the idea of human health.
fields.whyB: 'Clean and green' is a popular campaign slogan, not the constitutional wording.
fields.whyC: 'Safe and sanitary' sounds like health-code language, not Article II, Section 16.
fields.whyD: 'Productive and sustainable' echoes development policy terms, not the exact constitutional phrase.
fields.explanationTl: Sa Article II, Section 16, ang right ng tao ay sa isang 'balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.'
fields.hintTl: Dalawang idea ang pinagsama: balanse ng kalikasan at kalusugan ng tao.

reason: Key correct (RA 6713 Sec 4(A)(b)); replaced silly distractors (corruption, bribery) with plausible non-norms.

fields.text: Which of the following is one of the norms of conduct of public officials and employees under Section 4 of RA 6713?
fields.explanation: Section 4(A) of RA 6713 lists eight norms of conduct: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, and simple living. Professionalism is Section 4(A)(b).
fields.hint: Recall the norm about performing duties with excellence, intelligence and skill.
fields.whyB: RA 6713 requires the opposite, political neutrality: services are provided without partisanship.
fields.whyC: Seniority is a factor in some personnel actions, but it is not one of the eight norms in Section 4.
fields.whyD: The norms call for commitment to public interest above personal interest, not personal loyalty to superiors.
fields.explanationTl: Sa Section 4(A) ng RA 6713, walo ang norms of conduct, at isa dito ang professionalism: dapat excellent, competent at skilled ang pagganap sa trabaho.
fields.hintTl: Alalahanin mo yung norm tungkol sa pagtatrabaho nang may excellence at skill.

fields.text: Which inert gas is most commonly used to fill incandescent light bulbs to prevent the filament from oxidizing?
fields.explanation: Argon is the gas most commonly used to fill incandescent bulbs because it is inert, cheap and plentiful (about 1% of air), so it keeps the hot tungsten filament from reacting with oxygen.
fields.hint: It is the most abundant noble gas in Earth's air.
fields.whyA: Helium is inert but conducts heat away too fast and is not the usual bulb fill.
fields.whyC: Neon is known for glowing signs, not for filling ordinary incandescent bulbs.
fields.whyD: Hydrogen is not inert; it is flammable and is not used as a bulb fill.
fields.explanationTl: Argon ang karaniwang nilalagay sa incandescent bulb kasi inert ito, mura at marami sa hangin (mga 1%), kaya hindi nag-o-oxidize ang filament.
fields.hintTl: Ito ang pinakamaraming noble gas sa hangin natin.

fields.whyA: Hydrogen is the MOST abundant element, not the second.
fields.whyC: Oxygen is the third most abundant in the universe and the most abundant in Earth's crust.
fields.whyD: Carbon is common in living things but far less abundant than helium in the universe.
fields.explanationTl: Helium ang second most abundant element sa universe, kasunod ng hydrogen na number one.
fields.hintTl: Yung dalawang pinakamagaang element ay sila ring pinakamarami sa universe.

fields.explanation: The United States recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946 through the Treaty of Manila; June 12, 1898 was the declaration of independence from Spain.
fields.hint: It happened the year after World War II ended.
fields.whyB: 1898 is when independence from Spain was declared in Kawit, Cavite, not when the U.S. granted independence.
fields.whyC: 1935 is when the Commonwealth was inaugurated, a transition period before independence.
fields.whyD: 1965 has no link to independence; it is the year Ferdinand Marcos was first elected president.

fields.hintTl: Nangyari ito isang taon pagkatapos ng World War II.

fields.text: Boracay Island, famous for its white sand beaches, is part of which province?
fields.explanation: Boracay Island belongs to the municipality of Malay in the province of Aklan, Western Visayas, off the northwest tip of Panay.
fields.hint: It is the Panay province also known for the Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo.
fields.whyB: Antique is a neighbouring Panay province on the west coast, but Boracay is not part of it.
fields.whyC: Capiz is another Panay province, known as the seafood capital, not Boracay's province.
fields.whyD: Palawan is famous for El Nido and Coron beaches, not Boracay.
fields.explanationTl: Ang Boracay ay nasa bayan ng Malay, sa probinsya ng Aklan, Western Visayas, sa northwest tip ng Panay.
fields.hintTl: Ito yung probinsya sa Panay na sikat din sa Ati-Atihan festival sa Kalibo.

fields.text: Siargao Island, known as the 'Surfing Capital of the Philippines', is part of which province?
fields.explanation: Siargao Island, home of the Cloud 9 surf break, is part of the province of Surigao del Norte in the Caraga Region.
fields.hint: Its province shares the 'Surigao' name and lies at the northern tip of Mindanao.
fields.whyA: Surigao del Sur is a neighbouring province on the east coast of Mindanao, but Siargao is not part of it.
fields.whyB: Dinagat Islands is a separate island province in Caraga, north of Siargao, not Siargao's province.
fields.whyD: Agusan del Norte is a Caraga province on the Mindanao mainland, not Siargao's province.
fields.explanationTl: Ang Siargao, kung saan nandoon ang Cloud 9 surf break, ay part ng Surigao del Norte sa Caraga Region.
fields.hintTl: Ang probinsya nito ay may 'Surigao' sa pangalan at nasa northern tip ng Mindanao.
